solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cricketers in their season, we hear, ready to begin

definitions.note: the county cricket club of a south-west English county stands for its players

indicators.note: a listener's phrase, so the word for the cricketers' season is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: cricket is played in the summer
as in 'get set', poised to start

explanation.surface: A cricket team, in the middle of their summer, are poised to start play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes SUMMER sound like SOMER. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England with a first-class cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy: a county cricket club's name is used for its team of players.

clue.text: Clothes English band

parts.note: a strip is a sports team's kit

explanation.surface: An English group known for its outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: A team strip is the British word for its kit of shirt, shorts and socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stripe is a band or strip of colour.

clue.text: Wine capital

definitions.meaning: a sweet fortified wine made from a ... grape

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a sweet dessert wine and the chief city of Oman share the name.

clue.text: Commendation lacking at beginning, he will protest heatedly

indicators.note: the commendation word loses its opening letter

parts.note: praise is commendation
he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: Someone stripped of early praise vows to make a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking at beginning' drops P from PRAISE to leave RAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to raise hell is to make an angry, noisy protest.

clue.text: Axe trite "cigar" clue, poor

definitions.note: slang among rock musicians for a guitar

indicators.note: a poor version is a mangled one, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter scolds a hackneyed clue built around a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges TRITE CIGAR CLUE. 'Axe' is musicians' slang, not a chopping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: rock players call their instrument an axe, especially an amplified six-string.

clue.text: Charming of the French learner to take time in Europe!

parts.note: French 'du' means 'of the'
L is the learner driver's plate letter
CET is Central European Time

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a delightful French student who keeps continental hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dulcet tones are sweet and pleasing, so charming to the ear.

clue.text: Employment in America extremely gettable

parts.note: USA, the United States of America

indicators.note: takes the extreme letters, first and last, of gettable

explanation.surface: Jobs in the States are very easy to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: usage is the use or employment of something.

clue.text: Lady in France where exotic scents provide surroundings

indicators.note: the rearranged scents go around the French word
exotic means strange, so the letters of scents are rearranged

parts.note: French 'où' means 'where'

explanation.surface: A noblewoman in France wafts exotic perfumes about her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' is the anagram signal and 'provide surroundings' the containment: the jumbled perfume letters enclose the French for 'where', accent dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: a countess is a noblewoman, addressed as Lady in Britain.

clue.text: Article, golden, first for Einstein, say

parts.note: the is the definite article
or is gold in heraldry
1st, written IST, means first

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece names the golden physicist as number one.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written 1ST, read as the letters IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Einstein was a theoretical physicist, the archetype of someone who builds theories.

clue.text: Row where Earl Grey is? In reality it's trivial

parts.note: a storm is a violent row or uproar
Earl Grey is a blend of tea, served in a cup

explanation.surface: Is a quarrel over the tea service really all that serious?
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey is a bergamot-flavoured black tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a storm in a teacup is a great fuss about something unimportant.

clue.text: Note malice in break

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
spite is ill will or malice

explanation.surface: A musical note carries spite into a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a respite is a short rest or pause from something.

clue.text: Speak badly of business involving University College

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the business word wraps the college letters

parts.note: trade means commerce or business
UC is the standard abbreviation for University College

explanation.surface: Someone badmouths a commercial deal with a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to traduce someone is to slander or malign them.

clue.text: Quiet gym expert

parts.note: PE (physical education) is school gym class
an ace is a top expert

explanation.surface: A silent fitness instructor at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: peace and quiet both mean freedom from noise.

clue.text: He's annoying hill guide

definitions.note: a phrase for a person who annoys, standing for the noun

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
a mentor is an adviser or guide

explanation.surface: A grumble about a tiresome mountain guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent noun: a person who torments others is one who keeps pestering and vexing them.

clue.text: They challenge older views — visit seniors after review

indicators.note: a review reworks material, so the letters of the two words come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Iconoclasts go to see the elderly once a review is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' rearranges VISIT SENIORS; 'after' looks like a placing word but is part of the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: revisionists are people who reinterpret accepted history or doctrine.

clue.text: Shift dense smut — it's a necessity

indicators.note: to shift is to move about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Removing the thick grime is unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverb: 'needs must when the devil drives' says one does what is necessary.

clue.text: Sophisticated promotion? Very, with church included

parts.note: an ad promotes a product

indicators.note: the church letters are taken into the 'with' word

parts.note: and means together with
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: Is a smart career move enhanced by church membership?
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' looks like a career step, but it is an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: advanced means highly developed or sophisticated.

clue.text: Find daughter in built-up area after initially heading up north

indicators.note: the town piece comes after the initials
takes the first letter of each of the three words that follow
the daughter letter sits inside the town

parts.note: a town is a built-up area

explanation.surface: Tracking a daughter to a town after heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hunt down is to track and find someone after a search.

clue.text: Drink, happy about zone having been emptied, offering more protection

parts.note: a double is a double measure of spirits

indicators.note: about means around, so the happy word goes round the zone letters

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its outer letters, here of zone

explanation.surface: A cheerful drinker with a cleared area seems better shielded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been emptied' strips the middle of 'zone', and 'about' wraps the happy word round what remains. 'Drink' is a noun: a double measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: double-glazed windows have two panes, giving more insulation against cold and noise.

clue.text: Goodbye — is packing case

indicators.note: the farewell word packs the little word inside it

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A traveller says farewell while filling a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a valise is a small travelling bag or case.

clue.text: Somewhere to sleep, ultimately still before morning uproar

parts.note: a bed is where one sleeps

indicators.note: takes the last letter of still

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is morning

explanation.surface: Lying quietly in bed until a racket breaks out at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bedlam is a scene of noisy confusion, from the old London asylum.

clue.text: If ref late — unfortunately getting hell?

indicators.note: an unlucky outcome suggests things going awry, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tardy referee can expect a torrid time from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges IF REF LATE. The question mark marks hell as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: hell is one possible destination in the life believed to follow death.

clue.text: Old-time transport system getting new start

indicators.note: the opening letter of the transport word is swapped for another

parts.note: a metro is an urban railway system

explanation.surface: A vintage railway network is relaunched.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: retro describes styles imitating those of the past.

clue.text: Partners at table recalling long time trap

parts.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table

indicators.note: calling back suggests reading backwards, so the long-time word is reversed

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Bridge partners remember an old trick from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a snare is a noose or trap for catching animals.

clue.text: Country actor I recollected admiringly at first

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered up again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
takes only the opening letter of admiringly

explanation.surface: A performer fondly remembers a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' reads as remembered but means collected anew: ACTOR I rearranged gives CROATI, then A from 'admiringly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Croatia is a nation on the Adriatic coast of the Balkans.

clue.text: Decisive, rebuffing scoundrel, one in California

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the state abbreviation
rebuffing is pushing back, so the scoundrel word is turned round

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A firm Californian turns away a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffing' is the reversal signal and 'in' the containment; California's abbreviation here is the three-letter form, not CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a crucial moment is a decisive or critical one.

clue.text: Not entirely ascendant, one French Revolution figure

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who never quite rose to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Georges Danton was a leading figure of the French Revolution, guillotined in 1794.

clue.text: Against the current, having periods of success before time, leaves

parts.note: ups as in ups and downs
a ream is a quantity of sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Swimming against the tide after good spells, then departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is a noun: sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: going upstream means moving against the flow of a river.
